title: Why we need biased AI: How including cognitive and ethical machine biases can enhance AI systems

bias_targets.methodology: Theoretical evaluation of utilizing human cognitive heuristics (e.g., fast-and-frugal trees, take-the-best, and implicit regularization techniques like dropout) as inductive priors to reduce model complexity, prevent overfitting, and improve decision-making under uncertainty.

Theoretical proposal to intentionally filter social media training data to favor rational, reflective, and non-impulsive user interactions over affective, impulsive behavior in order to improve recommendation systems and public discourse.

Theoretical proposal to deliberately skew e-commerce training datasets to over-represent health-conscious and eco-conscious consumers, thereby training models to promote more sustainable purchasing behavior.

Theoretical proposal to intentionally exclude data showing risky, aggressive, or impulsive human driving behavior from autonomous vehicle training sets to strictly enforce safe and trustworthy autopilot behavior.

Theoretical proposal to restrict natural language generation training corpora to high-quality, editorially reviewed texts (rather than unfiltered public domain data) to prevent models from producing aggressive, discriminatory, or offensive language.
